lessons: Hook with an extreme comparative fact or paradigm shift rather than restating the title question (e.g., 'This shark is older than the United States' hit 1.85 retention at 10%, whereas repeating title questions like in the Potato video caused a 31.9% drop at 0.09s).

Never insert interactive pauses or countdowns like 'Pause and guess...', as they consistently trigger viewer drop-offs (e.g., drops occurred directly on 'Pause and guess...' in the Maple Syrup and 400 Degree Foil videos).
Cut redundant setup sentences immediately after the hook (e.g., stating 'They look like similar fruits' lost 30% of viewers at 0.13s; 'They are not just there to look cool' lost 31.5% at 0.11s).

Lead with tangible visual contrast over dense abstract mechanics (e.g., comparing red tuna to white cod held 86% vs. similar videos at the end, while abstract volume/nerve explanations in Fingers Prune and Leg Sleep collapsed below 10% final retention).
Avoid multi-clause defensive disclaimers mid-script (e.g., the long circulation/nerve disclaimer in the Leg Sleep video caused an immediate 29.3% drop).
worst_moment_types: Interactive pauses and countdown prompts (e.g., 'Pause and guess... three, two, one')
State-the-obvious filler sentences following the hook (e.g., 'They look like similar fruits')
Abstract hypotheticals asking viewers to mentalize mechanics (e.g., 'Now think about what happens when...')
Dense, multi-clause technical explanations immediately following the hook
best_hook_types: Extreme scale or historical anchors (e.g., 'This shark is older than the United States')
Challenging established paradigms or edge-of-knowledge facts (e.g., Pluto/Kuiper Belt boundaries)
Direct visual paradoxes between two familiar items (e.g., Red tuna vs. white cod meat)
